key_insight: Disordered silicon hosts harmonic vibrational modes with unusually large atomic displacement fluctuations, and these same local dynamics are tied to how heat flows through the material.
engineering_relevance: Understanding and mapping site-resolved lattice dynamics in amorphous silicon can guide thermal management and transport modeling in disordered semiconductor and glassy materials.
method: Use DFT-quality interatomic potentials to model realistic amorphous silicon networks.
Analyze harmonic vibrational modes and identify atoms with anomalously large root-mean-square positional variations.
Correlate atomic dynamics with site-projected thermal conductivity to link structure, motion, and heat transport.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports realistic-network simulations showing anomalously large RMS atomic displacement modes and a spatially resolved thermal-conductivity correlation, though no quantitative metrics are given here.
watch_item: Because the conclusion is drawn from modeled disordered networks and site-projected analysis, transferability to other materials and sensitivity to model realism should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Lattice dynamics of disordered phases of silicon and spatially resolved computations of thermal conductivity
